title: Create your first Task

body.text: Start by connecting a GitHub repo, then
write the instruction like a ticket for a teammate
— state the problem, where you think it's relevant, and the result you want. The clearer it is, the more on-target the AI.

example: "The submit button on /checkout has no loading state when clicked — add a spinner while waiting for the API and disable the button to prevent double clicks"

title: Write tasks so the AI performs well

body.text: context (what's broken/missing) + scope (which files it can touch) + success criteria (how to know it's done)
— add 'don't touch X' if there's an off-limits zone.

example: "Add phone-number validation to the signup form (10 digits, starting with 0), show an error under the field, don't change the API schema"

question: What do you need to do before creating your first task?

options.text: Connect a GitHub repo to Codex

question: What should a good task include?

options.text: The whole project's code pasted in

question: If there are files that must not be changed, what should you do?

options.text: Don't mention it — the AI will figure it out
State clearly in the instruction which files not to touch

question: How should you write tasks so Codex performs well?

options.text: Clearly state the goal, scope, and success conditions

question: What does a good task help with?

options.text: The AI understands and delivers work that matches your needs
